story.title: Tropical Storm Bertha Makes Landfall in Southern Louisiana
story.summary: Tropical Storm Bertha made landfall on southern Louisiana, approximately 40 miles east of New Orleans, bringing strong winds and prompting beach closures from the Florida Panhandle to Mississippi. The storm is now moving toward Texas as it continues to weaken.

event_overview.title: About Tropical Storms
event_overview.subject: Tropical Storms
event_overview.summary: This tracked event concerns concurrent tropical cyclones affecting two U.S. National Hurricane Center monitoring areas: Bertha in the Atlantic basin, including the Gulf Coast, and Fausto in the eastern North Pacific. Tropical storms are named tropical cyclones with sustained winds of 39–73 mph; once sustained winds reach 74 mph, they are classified as hurricanes.

facts.label: Seasonal timing
facts.value: The Atlantic hurricane season, which includes the Gulf of America, officially runs from June 1 through November 30; the eastern Pacific season runs from May 15 through November 30.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The eastern North Pacific basin is the portion of the North Pacific Ocean east of 140°W, while the Atlantic basin includes the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, and Gulf of America.

facts.label: Storm classifications
facts.value: A tropical storm has maximum sustained winds of 39–73 mph; a hurricane has maximum sustained winds of at least 74 mph. Major hurricanes are Category 3–5 systems, beginning at 111 mph.

facts.label: Forecasting authority
facts.value: NOAA’s National Hurricane Center in Miami is responsible for tracking tropical cyclones in both the Atlantic and eastern North Pacific and issues operational products including forecasts, public advisories, discussions, and wind-probability information for active cyclones.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: Bertha is on the 2026 Atlantic storm-name list. Tropical-cyclone names are assigned from rotating lists maintained through the World Meteorological Organization system.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the July 21–23, 2026 developments involving Bertha’s approach and reported landfall and Fausto’s concurrent eastern-Pacific development; it does not attempt to provide a complete storm lifecycle, full warning record, or final damage and casualty assessment.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground after landfall?
explore_lenses.title: Storm center shifted west; coastal disruptions persisted
explore_lenses.summary: Bertha came ashore in St. Bernard Parish on July 22 and by early July 23 was southwest of New Orleans, moving west. The immediate effects reported were concentrated in coastal access, surge-exposed areas and wind hazards rather than a confirmed broad damage assessment.

claims.text: Bertha made landfall around 2 p.m. CDT on July 22 in St. Bernard Parish, about 40 miles east of New Orleans, with reported sustained winds of 45 mph at landfall.
Early July 23, AP reported parks and piers closed along the coast and some low-lying roads closed; a tropical-storm warning still covered an area from Alabama to Louisiana, including New Orleans.
As of the early-July-23 report, the storm was about 110 miles southwest of New Orleans and moving west at 12 mph with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph.

points: Bertha made landfall around 2 p.m. CDT on July 22 in St. Bernard Parish, about 40 miles east of New Orleans, with reported sustained winds of 45 mph at landfall.
Early July 23, AP reported parks and piers closed along the coast and some low-lying roads closed; a tropical-storm warning still covered an area from Alabama to Louisiana, including New Orleans.
As of the early-July-23 report, the storm was about 110 miles southwest of New Orleans and moving west at 12 mph with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The consulted reports did not provide a final, independently verified accounting of damage, outages, injuries or flooding after landfall.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: Why did New Orleans avoid a direct core strike?
explore_lenses.title: The track stayed east and much of the worst weather remained offshore
explore_lenses.summary: The storm’s landfall east of New Orleans differed from early concerns that its path could cross the city. Louisiana officials described the response as a useful preparedness exercise, while stressing the city’s exposure to intense-rain events.

claims.text: Gov. Jeff Landry said initial projections raised concern that Bertha could track over New Orleans; he said the city is especially vulnerable to excessive-rainfall events.

Axios reported that the worst of the storm remained offshore after its St. Bernard Parish landfall; it characterized state officials as calling the preparations a 'dry run' for the remainder of hurricane season.
Landry said his office had increased coordination with the New Orleans Sewerage & Water Board after Hurricane Francine, including checking that pumps were staffed and operating.
Before landfall, National Hurricane Center official Jamie Rhome said strong wind shear could keep the worst of Bertha offshore, while forecasters still warned of coastal flooding and heavy rain.

explore_lenses.label: What hazards and operations remain for Texas?
explore_lenses.title: Upper Texas coast faced a continuing storm and marine threat
explore_lenses.summary: Forecasts on July 23 placed the remaining operational focus along south-central Louisiana and the upper Texas coast. Officials continued to warn that hazardous surf and marine conditions could outlast the storm center’s passage.

claims.text: The National Weather Service said Bertha was expected to continue affecting the northwestern Gulf Coast from south-central Louisiana to the upper Texas coast on July 23; a Small Craft Advisory was posted for waters southeast of Port O'Connor, Texas.
The National Hurricane Center forecast cited by AP expected Bertha to reach the upper Texas coast on July 23 and dissipate inland in Texas by July 24.

NHC’s tropical weather discussion said Bertha-generated swells would continue spreading west along the northern Gulf Coast for several days and were likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip-current conditions.

related_stories.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuation of Nearly 12,000 Tourists in Southwest France
related_stories.summary: A wildfire in Le Porge, southwest France, has led to the evacuation of nearly 12,000 people, primarily tourists. The fire, which began around midday on Wednesday, has prompted a significant response from hundreds of firefighters battling the flames. The region has been experiencing extreme heat, contributing to the wildfire's rapid spread.

related_stories.title: France Evacuates 20,000 Amid Wildfires in Southwestern Region
related_stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 people have been evacuated from towns and holiday resorts in southwestern France due to a raging wildfire near the coastal town of Lege Cap-Ferret. Most of those evacuated were tourists from campsites around Arcachon Bay in the Gironde region.

related_stories.title: FDA Advisory Committee Reviews Peptide Accessibility and Safety
related_stories.summary: An FDA advisory committee is convening to evaluate the accessibility and safety of over six peptides that have gained popularity as wellness treatments. Critics highlight the lack of sufficient data on their efficacy and safety, raising concerns about their promotion by influencers. The discussions aim to determine whether to ease restrictions on these substances.

related_stories.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Tankers Raise Oil Price Concerns
related_stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels, backed by Iran, have attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, raising concerns about the future of oil and gas prices. This incident may represent a new front in the ongoing conflict involving the US and Iran, prompting discussions on its potential economic impact, particularly on gas prices in the United States.
